title: How to schedule email in Gmail on Mac: step by step for Safari and Chrome
metaTitle: How to Schedule Email in Gmail on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to schedule email in gmail on mac in Safari or Chrome, find scheduled mail, edit it, and fix common send problems.
targetKeyword: how to schedule email in gmail on mac
intro: To schedule an email in Gmail on Mac, write it in Safari or Chrome, click the arrow next to Send, then choose Schedule send and pick a time. Google's help pages do not describe a Gmail app for Mac, so every step here runs in your browser.
tldr: Open Gmail at mail.google.com in Safari or Chrome, then click Compose.
Click the down arrow next to Send, choose Schedule send, and pick a date and time.
Find queued mail under Scheduled in the left panel.
To change a scheduled email, click Cancel send, edit the draft, and schedule it again.
Gmail holds up to 100 scheduled emails, and a send can run a few minutes late.

blocks.text: Gmail can hold a message and send it at a time you pick. That helps when a recipient is in another time zone, or when you finish a reply at the wrong time of day. The feature lives in Gmail on the web, so you use it in a browser on your Mac. I could not find a Gmail app for Mac on Google's help pages, so the steps in this guide use Safari or Chrome.
What you need before you start

You need a Gmail account and a web browser. Open mail.google.com and sign in before you start. The menu labels in this guide follow Google's help page for Gmail on a computer, so your screen should match them closely. Each step names the label you should see.
Check whether your account supports scheduling

A 2023 Apple Gazette article says scheduled send is not available to G Suite customers. Google's own help page does not say that. If you use a work account and the option is missing, ask your IT team before you spend more time on it. A personal Gmail account is the simplest test.
How the scheduling menu is laid out

The Send button sits at the bottom left of the compose window. A small down arrow sits right next to it. Google's help page labels that arrow More send options. Click the arrow, not the Send button, because Send delivers the message right away. Once the menu opens, you see Schedule send. The Apple Gazette article calls the same option Scheduled Send and mentions a Pick date & time choice, so your window may show either label.
Pick a time and check the time zone

Gmail sends at the time you choose, based on the time zone you select when you schedule. Google says a scheduled email may send a few minutes after the set time. Inbox Zero's troubleshooting guide adds that the time can differ from what you expect. The cause can be your account time zone, your device, your Google Calendar time zone, or travel.

Here is a case that catches people. You travel to another city and write a reminder from the hotel. Your Mac shows the local time, but your Google Calendar still uses home time. If you pick a time from the Mac clock, the email may land at a different hour than you intended for the person receiving it. Set the time for the zone you mean, and check it once more before you confirm.

blocks.title: Leave a little slack
blocks.text: Pick a time a few minutes before the moment that matters. Google says scheduled emails may send a few minutes after the set time, so a small buffer protects time sensitive messages.
Find, check, and change scheduled emails

Every message you schedule waits in one list. Click Scheduled in the left panel to open it. If you remember the subject or the recipient, type in:scheduled in the search bar instead, which the Apple Gazette article describes as a way to view scheduled mail. Open a message from the list to see its content and send time.

Cancel send changes the message back into a draft. It keeps your text, so you do not lose the work. Make your edits in the draft, then reschedule it from the arrow next to Send. Read the draft once more before you confirm. Check the recipients, the attachments, and the subject line, since the message is no longer waiting to go out.

blocks.text: Limits you should know before you rely on it

items: Up to 100 scheduled emails can wait at one time, according to Google's help page.
A scheduled email may send a few minutes after the time you set.
The send time follows the time zone you selected when you scheduled the message.
Scheduled mail in Gmail on the web is separate from Apple Mail's Send Later mailbox.

blocks.text: The 100 limit matters when you schedule a lot of mail in one batch, such as a series of follow-ups. Once the list is full, you have to send or cancel something before you can add more. Plan batches so the total stays under the cap. Spread the send times across the day, so you do not overload one recipient's inbox.
Quick checklist before you confirm
Run through this list in under a minute. Each item catches a mistake that is hard to fix once the message is queued.

items: Recipients and subject line are correct.
Any attachment you mention is attached.
The send time shows the time zone you meant.
Plain text mode is off, if you expected the schedule option.
The Scheduled list has room, since the cap is 100 messages.

blocks.text: Scheduling in Apple Mail instead

If your Gmail account lives in Apple Mail, Send Later works differently. Apple's Mail guide says to click the Send Later button and pick a time, or choose Send Later to set a date and time. The message moves to the Send Later mailbox in the sidebar. OS X Daily says the pull-down next to Send offers quick choices such as tonight or tomorrow morning, and that the feature needs macOS Ventura 13.0 or later.

The trade-off matters. Apple Mail sends the message from your Mac, so the Mac must be on and connected to the internet at the scheduled time. Inbox Zero notes that third-party clients such as Apple Mail do not use Gmail's server-side scheduling. To change a message, double-click it in the Send Later mailbox and click Edit at the top right. To stop it, select the message and click Delete.
Which method fits your work

Use Gmail in the browser if you already read mail there. Scheduling stays in one place, and Inbox Zero's note on server-side scheduling suggests the send does not depend on your Mac staying on. Use Apple Mail if your Gmail account already lives in Mail and you want the message to wait inside that app. Both paths work. Pick one and stick with it, so you always know where to look for queued mail.
Common mistakes people make

The first mistake is pressing ⌘ Enter, expecting it to schedule. That shortcut sends now. The second is editing a scheduled email in place. Inbox Zero says changing a scheduled email can cancel the send, so use Cancel send first. The third is trusting the clock on the wrong machine. Pick the time with the time zone in view, and recheck it before you confirm. Plain text mode can also hide the option, which catches people who expected it in the menu.
Keyboard shortcuts for scheduling in Gmail

Google's keyboard shortcut page lists no shortcut for scheduling. The closest one is ⌘ Enter, which sends the message immediately. Google's page also says shortcuts work differently on PCs and Macs, where Ctrl replaces ⌘. For moving around the mailbox, g + d opens Drafts. A scheduled email you cancel returns to Drafts, so that shortcut helps you find it again.
Worked example: a renewal reminder

Say you need to remind a client about a contract that renews at the end of the month. You write the note on a Friday afternoon, but you want it to arrive on Monday morning in the client's time zone. Click the arrow next to Send, choose Schedule send, and pick Monday morning. Confirm the time zone. Then check Scheduled before you leave on Friday, so you know the note is queued.

A second case is a follow-up after a call. You want it out during working hours, not during the call itself. Schedule it for the next morning, then read the draft once before you confirm. If you change your mind, click Cancel send, and the message returns to your drafts for another edit.
Scheduled send is not the same as undo send

People mix these two features up. Scheduled send holds a message until the time you pick. Undo send works after a message has already gone out, and it gives you a short window to pull it back. The two features solve different problems. For the undo steps, read [how to undo send in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/undo-send-in-gmail).
Troubleshooting checks before you give up

Most scheduling problems come from one of four things: the menu setting, the time zone, the way you edited the message, or the account type. Work through them in that order, since the first fix is the quickest. Start with the menu. Then check the time zone. Then check whether you edited the message in place. Last, check whether your account supports scheduling at all.
Next steps after you schedule your first email

Send yourself a test message first. Schedule it for a few minutes ahead, then check your inbox when it arrives. Once that works, you can trust the feature for client email. Keep an eye on Scheduled for your first week, so you learn what a waiting message looks like and when it goes out.

faq.question: Can I schedule email in Gmail on Mac without opening a browser?
faq.answer: I could not find a Gmail app for Mac on Google's help pages, so the scheduling steps run in Gmail on the web. Apple Mail has its own Send Later option. It works from the app on your Mac, but the Mac must be on and online at the send time.

faq.question: Where do I see the emails I scheduled?
faq.answer: Click Scheduled in the left panel of Gmail. You can also type in:scheduled in the search bar to find them.

faq.question: How do I cancel or change a scheduled email?
faq.answer: Open the message under Scheduled and click Cancel send at the top right. It turns back into a draft. Edit it, then click the arrow next to Send and choose Schedule send again.

faq.question: How many emails can I schedule at one time?
faq.answer: Google's help page says you can have up to 100 scheduled emails. Cancel or send some of them to make room for more.

faq.question: Will my scheduled email send at the exact minute?
faq.answer: Not always. Google says a scheduled email may send a few minutes after the set time. Give yourself a small buffer for anything time sensitive.

faq.question: Why is the Schedule send option missing?
faq.answer: Plain text mode can hide it. Turn plain text mode off from the three-dot More options menu. If the option still does not appear, a 2023 Apple Gazette article says the feature is not available to G Suite customers, so check with your admin.

faq.question: Does Apple Mail schedule email the same way as Gmail on the web?
faq.answer: No. Inbox Zero notes that third-party clients such as Apple Mail do not use Gmail's server-side scheduling. Apple Mail's Send Later needs macOS Ventura 13.0 or later and a Mac that is on and online at send time.

faq.question: Is scheduled send the same as undo send?
faq.answer: No. Scheduled send waits until the time you choose. Undo send works after a message has gone out. For the undo steps, read how to undo send in Gmail on Mac.

faq.question: Which time zone does Gmail use for a scheduled email?
faq.answer: Google says emails send based on the time zone you select when scheduling. If the time looks wrong, check your Mac clock and your Google Calendar default time zone.

task: Schedule an email in Gmail on a Mac
appliesTo: Gmail on the web in Safari or Chrome on macOS, plus Apple Mail notes
requirements: A Gmail account you can sign into at mail.google.com
Safari or Chrome on your Mac with Gmail open in a tab
For Apple Mail only: macOS Ventura 13.0 or later, and a Mac that is on and online at send time

steps.name: Open Gmail on the web
steps.text: Open Safari or Chrome on your Mac and go to mail.google.com. Sign in to the Gmail account you want to send from. Google's help page describes scheduling in Gmail on the web, so start there.
steps.tip: Scheduled mail goes out from the account you are signed into, so check the sender before you write.

steps.name: Write the message
steps.text: Click Compose. Add recipients, a subject, and your message in the new window. Review the text now, because you cancel the send later if you need to edit it.
steps.tip: A quick read before you schedule saves a cancel and reschedule later.

steps.name: Open the send options
steps.text: Look at the bottom left of the compose window. Click the small down arrow next to Send. Google's help page labels this arrow More send options.
steps.tip: Clicking the Send button itself sends the email right away. Only the arrow opens the schedule menu.

steps.name: Choose Schedule send
steps.text: Click Schedule send in the menu. The Apple Gazette article calls this option Scheduled Send, so use the label your window shows.
steps.tip: If you see a Pick date & time choice, click it to open the date and time picker.

steps.name: Pick the date and time
steps.text: Choose a time from the list, or pick your own date and time. Check the time zone before you go on, because Gmail sends based on the time zone you select when scheduling.
steps.tip: Choose a time that falls within working hours for the recipient, not just for you.

steps.name: Confirm the schedule
steps.text: Finish the dialog with the button that confirms the time. Google's help page says to choose a date and time but does not name the final button, so read the dialog before you click. A confirmed message waits under Scheduled until its send time.
steps.tip: If the message still sits in Drafts with no entry under Scheduled, repeat the menu steps and check again.

steps.name: Find your scheduled emails
steps.text: Click Scheduled in the left panel to see every message waiting to go out. To search for one, type in:scheduled in the search bar instead.
steps.tip: Gmail allows up to 100 scheduled emails, so the list can fill up on a busy day.

steps.name: Change a scheduled email
steps.text: Open the message under Scheduled and click Cancel send at the top right. It turns back into a draft. Make your changes, click the down arrow next to Send, choose Schedule send, and set a new time.
steps.tip: Do not edit a scheduled message in place. Cancel send first, or the send can stop.

troubleshooting.problem: Schedule send is missing from the send menu
troubleshooting.fix: Plain text mode can hide it. Open the three-dot More options menu at the bottom of the compose window and turn plain text mode off. Then click the arrow next to Send again.

troubleshooting.problem: The email went out at the wrong hour
troubleshooting.fix: Check the time zone you selected when you scheduled. Then check your Mac clock and your Google Calendar default time zone. Inbox Zero lists the account, device, Calendar, and travel time zones as possible causes.

troubleshooting.problem: The scheduled email did not send on time
troubleshooting.fix: Google says a scheduled email may send a few minutes after the set time. Wait a short while before you assume a failure. If the message is still under Scheduled after that, open it and check the send time.

troubleshooting.problem: I edited a scheduled email and the send stopped
troubleshooting.fix: Changing a scheduled email can cancel the send. Open it under Scheduled, click Cancel send, make your edits, then reschedule from the arrow next to Send.

troubleshooting.problem: Gmail says I have too many scheduled emails
troubleshooting.fix: Gmail allows up to 100 scheduled emails. Open Scheduled, cancel or send the ones you no longer need, then schedule the new message again.

troubleshooting.problem: Apple Mail did not send my Send Later message
troubleshooting.fix: Check that your Mac was on and online at the scheduled time, and that it runs macOS Ventura 13.0 or later. Apple Mail depends on the Mac, unlike Gmail's own scheduling.
